newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian bourse head praises re-election vote.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian bourse head praises re-election vote.

text.p: The head of South America's largest stock market praised the Brazilian Congress' preliminary passage of a re-election constitutional amendment but said the government now must work hard to implement economic reforms.
"The re-election amendment's approval opens up a more concrete horizon of stability," Alfredo Rizkallah, president of the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa), said in a statement.
But, he added, the government's political victory in getting the Chamber of Deputies to pass the bill Tuesday night comes with a "great responsibility."

"The government...must use all of its political energy to promote desired reforms, particularly those which will eliminate the public deficit, because (that) is the major obstacle to greater stability" in Brazil, he said.
Rizkallah said increased stability will encourage greater savings, which he called the "motor" for investment, development, jobs creation, higher exports and other positive economic trends.
The constitutional amendment, which would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso stand for an unprecedented second term in 1998, faces a second lower house vote as well as two votes in the Senate.

Investors favor re-election because it promises political continuity and progress in getting Congress to pass pension, fiscal and administrative deemed crucial to Cardoso's Real economic stabilization plan.

The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index, which was up a sharp 10 percent since the year began on optimism the amendment would be passed by Congress, dropped on profit-taking after Tuesday night's chamber vote.
